Title: Whine Bitch Moan Complain games starting up -- interested?

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
Gang,
I'm starting up a few JOL games with some new rules. I'd encourage (though not require) you to make decks with some of these cards, to see what will happen with the changes.

Please reply in this thread with your JOL nick if you wish to participate in this experiment.

When we have enough players, I'll begin the games starting the second week in June.

RULES  Section [5] in the rulebook says "A Methuselah may not have more than two Master Phase Actions."

COSTS  Deflection costs 1 pool.
Govern costs 2 blood.
Conditioning costs 2 blood.

TEXT
----
Master:Discipline cards read "Master:Discipline. Trifle."

Trophies EXCEPT FOR Trophy:Progeny all read "Master:Trifle."

Archetypes EXCEPT FOR Perfectionist all read "Master:Trifle."

Ashur Tablets reads "...choose up to three cards..."

Pentex Subversion(TM) reads "Each Methuselah may play only one Pentex Subversion(TM) in a game."

Parity Shift reads "Each Methuselah may play or call only one Parity Shift in a game."

BANNED  Direct Intervention is banned.

Even that would be a big change. It mean significantly slower oust and build-up via dominate.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: In my opinion, very few cards are worth more than 1 blood. There are plenty of other discplines that have +2 bleed actions that cost 1 blood, some even that are free, so why should govern be nerfed like that?

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> Klaital wrote:
> In my opinion, very few cards are worth more than 1 blood. There are plenty of other discplines that have +2 bleed actions that cost 1 blood, some even that are free, so why should govern be nerfed like that?
>
'cause he is by a fair margin the best one, for two reason :
* he is in dominate, with other very good defensive and offensive option, like Conditionning and Deflection. A  weenie is far superior to a  weenie (or even a  weenie in fact) because of this.
* he have an alternate sup' level which is useful and very different. Unlike the presence version, you can actually deal with your prey/predator so that they don't block a govern sup, for example.

That does not mean that the change used in this thread are the best. It's just that the goal is to hit hard the dominate, and to do this you have to hit either Conditionning, Govern, or Deflection with a big hammer. Here, all three are hit.

Messages.Author: Klaital
Messages.Body: I already use Redirection instead of Deflection in most of my dominate decks anyway, because its silly to pay for something you can get for free, and most of my decks don't leave vampires loitering untapped anyway. Also if you nerf conditioning, people just move to using threats or foreshadowing, which I already use in many decks over conditioning since again, free is good.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> Klaital wrote:
> I already use Redirection instead of Deflection in most of my dominate decks anyway, because its silly to pay for something you can get for free, and most of my decks don't leave vampires loitering untapped anyway. Also if you nerf conditioning, people just move to using threats or foreshadowing, which I already use in many decks over conditioning since again, free is good.
>
Well, it's more "argument to also nerf Redirection, threat, and foreshadowing destruction" than anything else

More seriously, Redirection, like every bounce accessible with an inferior discipline, is problematic, while threat and foreshadowing are both actually quite a bit less good than conditionning (but better than 2-blood conditionning) simply because 1 blood for an unconditionnal +2/+3 is just better than being free and having restriction or less bleed.

If dominate had neither govern, conditionning, nor bleed redirection, the "dominate module" would not be a successful concept
